source_cards.title: Beyond Dry References: Learning Relative Audio Effects Representations via Contrastive Distance Learning
source_cards.key_revision: The headline base model is hybrid differential-plus-absolute fusion; the published ablations do not isolate pure relative fusion.

source_cards.title: ST-ITO: Controlling Audio Effects for Style Transfer with Inference-Time Optimization
source_cards.bounded_conclusion: Effect-aware objectives can guide optimization, but learned similarity alone does not establish preference; simple rule-based methods can remain competitive on simple styles and guitar-tone matching is a reported failure mode.

positive_checks: non-finite final renders rejected and partial output removed
float output and weighted mixing tested
sidechain and splitter REAPER integration cases present
silent and non-finite preset candidates rejected
remaining_gaps: RMS activity is not parameter or graph correctness
no explicit true-peak loudness latency-compensation or state-recall gate
default three-second tail is not measured decay completion

knowledge_cards.claim: RelFx Base is hybrid relative-plus-absolute fusion.
The single-branch ablation does not isolate the causal contribution of pure relative fusion.
Architectural antisymmetry is not processor invertibility.
Ground-truth restart selection is oracle reranking and must be separated from deployable selection.
Median benchmark gains without uncertainty or listening tests do not establish rock-mix preference.
Dry-reference-free training does not imply dry-free or topology-free deployment validation.
Learned effect similarity can be optimized without guaranteeing superior listener judgement.
WildFX current tests reject several invalid-output classes and should not be described as load-only.
Non-silent RMS is an activity gate, not a render-equivalence gate.
A fixed render tail must not substitute for measured decay completion.
